## macos-harness

```text
OVERVIEW: Let agents see and operate macOS apps.

Commands talk to the macOS Harness menu bar helper, which holds the Screen Recording and
Accessibility permissions. The helper starts automatically.

USAGE: macos-harness <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

SUBCOMMANDS:
  doctor                  Check that the helper runs, has its permissions, and knows who is calling.
  apps                    List running apps.
  windows                 List windows, with the IDs other commands take.
  snapshot                Show a window's UI as a tree of elements with refs (e12) and click points.
  find                    Find elements by text, role or identifier, including ones scrolled out of
                          view.
  read                    Read an element in full: its whole label and value, the text inside it,
                          and its links.
  collect                 Gather every item of a long list, scrolling it, and print each item once
                          with its text and links.
  screenshot              Capture one window as PNG. Never includes other apps' windows.
  menu                    Show an app's menus with shortcuts and enabled state, or its menu bar
                          extras.
  press                   Press a button, checkbox, tab, menu button or any element with a press
                          action (through AX; your cursor stays put).
  set-value               Set a text field, slider, checkbox or other value directly.
  type                    Type text at the cursor of the focused element (or --into a ref), without
                          moving your cursor.
  paste                   Paste text at the cursor of the focused element (or --into a ref) through
                          the clipboard, for apps that ignore typing; your clipboard is put back.
  key                     Send a key or shortcut to an app, e.g. return, esc, cmd+s, ⇧⌘N (letters
                          and digits follow the current keyboard layout).
  focus                   Give an element keyboard focus.
  select                  Select a row, tab or item.
  scroll-to               Scroll an element into view.
  increment               Step a slider or stepper up.
  decrement               Step a slider or stepper down.
  menu-select             Choose a menu item by path, e.g. menu-select -a TextEdit Format Font Bold.
  window                  Activate, move, resize, minimize, restore, full-screen or close a window.
  launch                  Launch an app (in the background unless --activate) and wait for its
                          first window.
  quit                    Quit an app (asks it nicely unless --force).
  wait                    Wait until an element appears (or with --gone, disappears).
  click                   Click an element or point: in the background when the window takes it,
                          else with the real mouse. Prefer `press` when the element has an AX
                          action.
  hover                   Move the real cursor over an element and stay, for tooltips and hover
                          states.
  drag                    Drag with the real mouse from an element or point to another (moving
                          files, chess pieces, sliders).
  scroll                  Scroll over an element or point, in pixels: in the background when the
                          window takes it, else with the real wheel.
  swipe                   Swipe with the real mouse: press, move the given distance, release. On a
                          simulator this is a finger swipe.
  long-press              Press and hold with the real mouse: a long press on a simulator, a held
                          click on the Mac.
  sim                     Start, stop and set up iOS Simulators, and run apps on them.
  android                 Start and stop Android emulators, run apps on emulators and phones, and
                          change their settings.
  build                   Build an app with xcodebuild for the iOS Simulator or this Mac, and
                          optionally run it.
  journal                 List agent sessions from the journal, or show one session's requests
                          (typed text is never recorded).
  steps                   Run several steps in one call, written like a flow's steps, and report
                          each step and the changes they made.
  clipboard               Show what's on the clipboard: its types and its text (not text a password
                          manager concealed).
  flow                    Run and check UI flows: YAML files of steps with expectations.
  record                  Record an app's windows to a movie, and pull stills out of it.
  setup                   Connect an agent: register the MCP server with Claude Code, Codex,
                          Cursor, Gemini CLI or opencode, or install the skill for pi.
  mcp                     Run as an MCP server on stdin/stdout (for Claude Code, Codex and other
                          MCP hosts).

  See 'macos-harness help <subcommand>' for detailed help.
```

## macos-harness doctor

```text
OVERVIEW: Check that the helper runs, has its permissions, and knows who is calling.

USAGE: macos-harness doctor [--report] [--out <out>] [--include-titles] [--json]

OPTIONS:
  --report                Write a bug report to a text file instead: versions, this check, recent
                          errors and the latest journal session (no typed text or screenshots).
  --out <out>             Where --report writes (default: macos-harness-report-<time>.txt here).
  --include-titles        Keep window titles and element labels in the --report (left out by
                          default).
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness apps

```text
OVERVIEW: List running apps.

USAGE: macos-harness apps [--all] [--json]

OPTIONS:
  --all                   Include menu bar agents and background processes.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness windows

```text
OVERVIEW: List windows, with the IDs other commands take.

USAGE: macos-harness windows [--app <app>] [--json]

OPTIONS:
  -a, --app <app>         Only this app (name, bundle ID or pid).
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness snapshot

```text
OVERVIEW: Show a window's UI as a tree of elements with refs (e12) and click points.

Refs stay valid while the element exists, and later commands accept them. Coordinates are
window-relative points. --since last shows only what changed since your previous snapshot of the
window (with the same --root and limits); --query keeps only matching elements and the elements
they're in.

USAGE: macos-harness snapshot --app <app> [--window <window>] [--root <root>] [--max-nodes <max-nodes>] [--max-depth <max-depth>] [--since <since>] [--query <query>] [--links] [--json]

OPTIONS:
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --root <root>           Start from this ref, e.g. to expand a node marked "+N more".
  --max-nodes <max-nodes> Most elements to show. (default: 250)
  --max-depth <max-depth> Deepest level to show. (default: 40)
  --since <since>         last: show only what changed since your previous snapshot of this window.
  --query <query>         Show only elements whose label, value or identifier contains this, and
                          the elements they're in.
  --links                 Show where each link goes (a web page's own address is always shown).
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness find

```text
OVERVIEW: Find elements by text, role or identifier, including ones scrolled out of view.

USAGE: macos-harness find [<text>] --app <app> [--window <window>] [--role <role>] [--id <id>] [--exact] [--limit <limit>] [--ocr] [--links] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <text>                  Text to match against label, value or identifier.

OPTIONS:
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --role <role>           Role, e.g. button, textfield, AXCheckBox.
  --id <id>               Exact accessibility identifier.
  --exact                 Match the whole text instead of a substring.
  --limit <limit>         Most matches to return. (default: 20)
  --ocr                   Look for the text in the window's pixels with text recognition (for text
                          the tree doesn't have); without text, list every line read.
  --links                 Show where each matching link goes.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness read

```text
OVERVIEW: Read an element in full: its whole label and value, the text inside it, and its links.

Snapshots and find shorten long labels and values; read gives them whole, with all the text inside
the element in reading order (a post's author, text and counts, say) and where each link inside it
goes. Without an element it reads the whole window.

USAGE: macos-harness read [<ref>] --app <app> [--window <window>] [--text <text>] [--role <role>] [--id <id>] [--exact] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <ref>                   Ref from snapshot or find, e.g. k12.

OPTIONS:
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --text <text>           Match label, value or identifier containing this text.
  --role <role>           Role, e.g. group, link, textarea.
  --id <id>               Exact accessibility identifier.
  --exact                 --text must match the whole label, value or identifier.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness collect

```text
OVERVIEW: Gather every item of a long list, scrolling it, and print each item once with its text
and links.

For lists that show only part of themselves at a time: web timelines and feeds, long tables, iOS
and Android lists. Name the items with --role (article for a web page's posts, row, cell), --text
or --id. It scrolls by bringing the last item into view, or a background scroll, never the real
mouse, and stops at --max, --until, the end of the list, or after --max-seconds; --continue then
carries on without repeating items.

USAGE: macos-harness collect [<options>] --app <app>

OPTIONS:
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --role <role>           Role of the items, e.g. article, row, cell.
  --text <text>           The items' label, value or identifier contains this text.
  --id <id>               The items' exact accessibility identifier.
  --exact                 --text must match the whole label, value or identifier.
  --within <within>       Ref of the list or scroll area to read and scroll (default: the window).
  --key <key>             Tell items apart by their first link whose URL contains this (e.g.
                          /status/) instead of by their text.
  --max <max>             Most items to return (at most 500). (default: 50)
  --until <until>         Stop after the first item whose text contains this.
  --max-seconds <max-seconds>
                          Longest time to keep scrolling, in seconds. (default: 45.0)
  --continue              Leave out items this session already got from this list.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness screenshot

```text
OVERVIEW: Capture one window as PNG. Never includes other apps' windows.

Prints the file path. Window-relative point = pixel / scale (plus the crop origin when cropped).

USAGE: macos-harness screenshot --app <app> [--window <window>] [--element <element>] [--max-size <max-size>] [--labels] [--grid <grid>] [--out <out>] [--json]

OPTIONS:
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --element <element>     Crop to this element's ref.
  --max-size <max-size>   Longest edge in pixels; 0 keeps full resolution. (default: 1600)
  --labels                Draw ref labels on the elements you can act on.
  --grid <grid>           Draw a grid of window coordinates every this many points (for canvases
                          without a tree).
  -o, --out <out>         Where to write the PNG; defaults to a temporary file, deleted after an
                          hour.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness menu

```text
OVERVIEW: Show an app's menus with shortcuts and enabled state, or its menu bar extras.

With no path, lists the menu bar. `menu -a TextEdit File` lists the File menu.
With --extras, lists the app's menu bar extras (status items on the right of the menu bar), e.g.
`menu --extras -a "Control Center"` for most of the system's own (others belong to SystemUIServer).
`menu --extras -a App Extra` presses that extra, lists the menu it shows and closes it again.

USAGE: macos-harness menu [<path> ...] --app <app> [--depth <depth>] [--extras] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <path>                  Menu titles to descend through, e.g. File "Open Recent"; with --extras,
                          an extra's name first (optional when the app has one).

OPTIONS:
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid.
  --depth <depth>         Levels to show below the path. (default: 1)
  --extras                Read the app's menu bar extras (status items) instead of its menu bar.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness press

```text
OVERVIEW: Press a button, checkbox, tab, menu button or any element with a press action (through
AX; your cursor stays put).

USAGE: macos-harness press [<ref>] [--text <text>] [--role <role>] [--id <id>] [--exact] [--ocr] --app <app> [--window <window>] [--no-diff] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <ref>                   Ref from snapshot or find, e.g. k12.

OPTIONS:
  --text <text>           Match label, value or identifier containing this text.
  --role <role>           Role, e.g. button, textfield, switch, tab.
  --id <id>               Exact accessibility identifier.
  --exact                 --text must match the whole label, value or identifier.
  --ocr                   Find --text in the window's pixels with text recognition (for the pointer
                          commands).
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --no-diff               Don't wait for the UI to settle or report changes.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness set-value

```text
OVERVIEW: Set a text field, slider, checkbox or other value directly.

USAGE: macos-harness set-value [<ref>] [--text <text>] [--role <role>] [--id <id>] [--exact] [--ocr] --value <value> --app <app> [--window <window>] [--no-diff] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <ref>                   Ref from snapshot or find, e.g. k12.

OPTIONS:
  --text <text>           Match label, value or identifier containing this text.
  --role <role>           Role, e.g. button, textfield, switch, tab.
  --id <id>               Exact accessibility identifier.
  --exact                 --text must match the whole label, value or identifier.
  --ocr                   Find --text in the window's pixels with text recognition (for the pointer
                          commands).
  -v, --value <value>     The new value.
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --no-diff               Don't wait for the UI to settle or report changes.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness type

```text
OVERVIEW: Type text at the cursor of the focused element (or --into a ref), without moving your
cursor.

USAGE: macos-harness type <text> [--into <into>] [--real] --app <app> [--window <window>] [--no-diff] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <text>                  The text to type.

OPTIONS:
  --into <into>           Ref of the element to type into; defaults to the app's focused element.
  --real                  Send real keystrokes to the frontmost app (for apps that ignore the other
                          ways).
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --no-diff               Don't wait for the UI to settle or report changes.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

```text

```

```text
  <ref>                   Ref from snapshot or find, e.g. k12.

OPTIONS:
  --text <text>           Match label, value or identifier containing this text.
  --role <role>           Role, e.g. button, textfield, switch, tab.
  --id <id>               Exact accessibility identifier.
  --exact                 --text must match the whole label, value or identifier.
  --ocr                   Find --text in the window's pixels with text recognition (for the pointer
                          commands).
```
```text
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --no-diff               Don't wait for the UI to settle or report changes.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness menu-select

```text
OVERVIEW: Choose a menu item by path, e.g. menu-select -a TextEdit Format Font Bold.

Brings the app to the front first (most menu items act on its key window); your cursor doesn't
move.
With --extras, chooses from one of the app's menu bar extras (status items) instead, without
bringing it to the front: `menu-select --extras -a App Extra "Settings…"`. The extra's name may be
left out when the app has only one, and a path of just the extra presses it (for extras that open a
window or act on a click).

USAGE: macos-harness menu-select [<path> ...] --app <app> [--no-activate] [--extras] [--no-diff] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <path>                  Menu titles down to the item; with --extras, the extra's name first.

OPTIONS:
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid.
  --no-activate           Don't bring the app to the front first.
  --extras                Choose from the app's menu bar extras (status items) instead of its menu
                          bar.
  --no-diff               Don't wait for the UI to settle or report changes.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```


## macos-harness launch

```text
OVERVIEW: Launch an app (in the background unless --activate) and wait for its first window.

USAGE: macos-harness launch <app> [--open <open> ...] [--arg <arg> ...] [--env <env> ...] [--activate] [--new-instance] [--appearance <appearance>] [--language <language>] [--locale <locale>] [--allow-idle-when-covered] [--timeout <timeout>] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <app>                   App name, bundle ID or path to an .app.

OPTIONS:
  --open <open>           A file to open with it (repeatable).
  --arg <arg>             A launch argument (repeatable); write values starting with - as
                          --arg=--flag.
  --env <env>             KEY=VALUE environment variable (repeatable).
  --activate              Bring it to the front.
  --new-instance          Start another copy even if it's running (for a browser with its own
                          profile); target it by its pid.
  --appearance <appearance>
                          Launch it in light or dark mode, whatever the system's set to.
  --language <language>   Launch it in this language, e.g. fr or pt-BR.
  --locale <locale>       Launch it with this locale, e.g. fr_FR.
  --allow-idle-when-covered
                          Chromium and Electron apps are launched so they keep working when other
                          windows cover them; this leaves that off.
  --timeout <timeout>     Seconds to wait for a window. (default: 15.0)
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness click

```text
OVERVIEW: Click an element or point: in the background when the window takes it, else with the real
mouse. Prefer `press` when the element has an AX action.

The click goes to the window in the background, without moving your cursor or bringing the app
forward. If nothing visibly changes, it isn't repeated (it may have worked out of sight; a
backgroundUnconfirmed notice says so): repeat it with --real if it didn't take. Text fields, text
views and sheets, which ignore background clicks, get the real mouse straight away. The real mouse
brings the app to the front, waits until you're not using the mouse or keyboard, refuses if another
app's window covers the point, and puts your cursor back. Clicks with --modifiers always use it,
and so does every click while the user has clicks and scrolls in the background turned off in the
menu bar panel's settings.

USAGE: macos-harness click [<options>] [<ref>] --app <app>

ARGUMENTS:
  <ref>                   Ref from snapshot or find, e.g. k12.

OPTIONS:
  --text <text>           Match label, value or identifier containing this text.
  --role <role>           Role, e.g. button, textfield, switch, tab.
  --id <id>               Exact accessibility identifier.
  --exact                 --text must match the whole label, value or identifier.
  --ocr                   Find --text in the window's pixels with text recognition (for the pointer
                          commands).
  --x <x>                 Window-relative x in points; the device's points for sim:, pixels for
                          android: (instead of an element).
  --y <y>                 Window-relative y in points; the device's points for sim:, pixels for
                          android: (instead of an element).
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --right                 Right-click (opens context menus; their items come back as refs).
  --count <count>         Clicks: 2 for a double-click. (default: 1)
  --real                  Use the real mouse without trying the background first.
  --modifiers <modifiers> Keys held during the action, comma-separated: cmd,shift,opt,ctrl.
  --no-diff               Don't wait for the UI to settle or report changes.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness drag

```text
OVERVIEW: Drag with the real mouse from an element or point to another (moving files, chess pieces,
sliders).

Stops and releases the button if you move the mouse, type or press ⌃⌥⌘. partway. To end in another
window or app, name it with --to-app and --to-window; --to, --to-text and --to-x/--to-y are then in
that window. That window is raised behind the app the drag starts in, and the drag is refused if
anything covers the drop point.

USAGE: macos-harness drag [<options>] [<ref>] --app <app>

ARGUMENTS:
  <ref>                   Ref from snapshot or find, e.g. k12.

OPTIONS:
  --text <text>           Match label, value or identifier containing this text.
  --role <role>           Role, e.g. button, textfield, switch, tab.
  --id <id>               Exact accessibility identifier.
  --exact                 --text must match the whole label, value or identifier.
  --ocr                   Find --text in the window's pixels with text recognition (for the pointer
                          commands).
  --x <x>                 Window-relative x in points; the device's points for sim:, pixels for
                          android: (instead of an element).
  --y <y>                 Window-relative y in points; the device's points for sim:, pixels for
                          android: (instead of an element).
  --to <to>               Destination ref (from the destination app with --to-app).
  --to-text <to-text>     Destination: element containing this text.
  --to-role <to-role>     Destination: role.
  --to-id <to-id>         Destination: identifier.
  --to-x <to-x>           Destination x, relative to the destination window.
  --to-y <to-y>           Destination y, relative to the destination window.
  --to-app <to-app>       End the drag in this app (name, bundle ID or pid); defaults to -a.
  --to-window <to-window> End the drag in this window ID from `windows`; defaults to the
                          destination app's focused window.
  --hold <hold>           Seconds to hold before moving (helps drag-and-drop start). (default: 0.3)
  --duration <duration>   Seconds the move takes. (default: 0.6)
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --modifiers <modifiers> Keys held during the action, comma-separated: cmd,shift,opt,ctrl.
  --no-diff               Don't wait for the UI to settle or report changes.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness sim

```text
OVERVIEW: Start, stop and set up iOS Simulators, and run apps on them.

To see and operate a simulator's screen, use the usual commands with `-a sim:<device>`, e.g.
`snapshot -a sim:booted` or `press -a "sim:iPhone 18 Pro" --text Settings`. A device is a UDID, a
name, or `booted` for the only booted simulator. Needs Xcode 27 or later.

USAGE: macos-harness sim <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

SUBCOMMANDS:
  list                    List the available simulators, booted ones first.
  boot                    Boot a simulator, wait until it's ready, and show it in Device Hub.
  shutdown                Shut a simulator down.
  install                 Install a built .app on a simulator.
  uninstall               Remove an app from a simulator.
  launch                  Start an app on a simulator (restarting it if it's running).
  terminate               Stop an app running on a simulator.
  open-url                Open a URL on a simulator: a web page, a deep link or a universal link.
  button                  Press a hardware button or turn the device.
  privacy                 Grant, revoke or reset an app's access to photos, location, camera and
                          the like.
  push                    Send a push notification to an app on a simulator.
  location                Set or clear a simulator's location.
  appearance              Switch a simulator to light or dark mode.
  status-bar              Show fixed status bar values (for clean screenshots), or clear them.
  pasteboard              Put text on a simulator's pasteboard, or read what's there.

  See 'macos-harness help sim <subcommand>' for detailed help.
```

```text
USAGE: macos-harness sim push <device> <bundle-id> <payload> [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <device>                The simulator: a UDID, a name, or `booted`.
  <bundle-id>             The app's bundle ID.
  <payload>               A JSON file with the payload, or - for standard input.

OPTIONS:
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness sim status-bar

```text
OVERVIEW: Show fixed status bar values (for clean screenshots), or clear them.

USAGE: macos-harness sim status-bar <device> [--clear] [--time <time>] [--battery <battery>] [--battery-state <battery-state>] [--wifi <wifi>] [--cellular <cellular>] [--network <network>] [--carrier <carrier>] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <device>                The simulator: a UDID, a name, or `booted`.

OPTIONS:

  --cellular <cellular>   Cellular bars, 0–4.
  --network <network>     Data network: wifi, 3g, 4g, lte, lte-a, lte+, 5g, 5g+, 5g-uwb, 5g-uc…
  --carrier <carrier>     Carrier name.
```


## macos-harness android

```text
OVERVIEW: Start and stop Android emulators, run apps on emulators and phones, and change their
settings.

To see and operate a device's screen, use the usual commands with `-a android:<device>`, e.g.
`snapshot -a android:booted` or `press -a android:emulator-5554 --text Settings`. A device is an
adb serial, an emulator's name, a phone's model, or `booted` for the only running device.
Coordinates are the screen's pixels. Needs the Android SDK (adb).

USAGE: macos-harness android <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

SUBCOMMANDS:
  list                    List connected devices and emulators, running ones first.
  boot                    Start an emulator and wait until Android has booted.
  shutdown                Shut an emulator down.
  install                 Install an .apk (or replace the installed one).
  uninstall               Remove an app.
  launch                  Start an app's launcher activity (restarting it if it's running).
  terminate               Stop an app.
  open-url                Open a URL: a web page or an app link.
  button                  Press a system button, or pull down the notifications.
  permission              Grant or revoke an app's runtime permission, or revoke all of them.
  location                Set an emulator's location.
  appearance              Switch to light or dark mode.
  rotate                  Turn the screen, or let it follow the device again.
  status-bar              Show a clean status bar (demo mode) for screenshots, or go back to the
                          real one.

  See 'macos-harness help android <subcommand>' for detailed help.
```

```text
OVERVIEW: List connected devices and emulators, running ones first.
```


## macos-harness build

```text
OVERVIEW: Build an app with xcodebuild for the iOS Simulator or this Mac, and optionally run it.

Finds the .xcworkspace or .xcodeproj in this folder unless you name one. Builds for the iOS
Simulator when the scheme has one, and for this Mac otherwise or with --mac: natively when the
scheme supports macOS, as Mac Catalyst when that's how it runs on a Mac. The full log goes to
~/Library/Logs/macos-harness/builds.

USAGE: macos-harness build [--project <project>] [--workspace <workspace>] [--scheme <scheme>] [--configuration <configuration>] [--device <device>] [--mac] [--run] [--verbose] [--json]

OPTIONS:
  --project <project>     The .xcodeproj to build.
  --workspace <workspace> The .xcworkspace to build.
  --scheme <scheme>       The scheme (default: the only one).
  --configuration <configuration>
                          Build configuration. (default: Debug)
  --device <device>       Build for this simulator (UDID, name or booted); default: any simulator.
  --mac                   Build for this Mac (natively or as Mac Catalyst) even when the scheme has
                          a simulator.
  --run                   After a successful build, run the app: install and launch it on --device,
                          or on this Mac quit any running copy and launch the new build.
  --verbose               Print xcodebuild's output as it goes.
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness journal

```text
OVERVIEW: List agent sessions from the journal, or show one session's requests (typed text is never
recorded).

USAGE: macos-harness journal [<session>] [--limit <limit>] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <session>               A session ID from the list, or `last` for the newest.

OPTIONS:
  --limit <limit>         Most sessions to list. (default: 20)
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness steps

```text
OVERVIEW: Run several steps in one call, written like a flow's steps, and report each step and the
changes they made.

Steps are a YAML list, e.g. '[{press: {id: Seven}}, {press: {id: Multiply}}, {press: {id: Six}},
{press: {id: Equals}}]', or - to read them from standard input. They run in order and stop at the
first failure; each goes through the same checks as its own command. Up to 64 steps. Shell, build,
launch, quit, screenshot, sim and android steps aren't allowed here; put those in a flow.

USAGE: macos-harness steps <steps> --app <app> [--window <window>] [--observe <observe>] [--max-nodes <max-nodes>] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <steps>                 The steps as a YAML list, or - to read them from standard input.

OPTIONS:
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --observe <observe>     What to report afterwards: changes, snapshot or none. (default: changes)
  --max-nodes <max-nodes> Most elements in the snapshot. (default: 250)
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness flow

```text
OVERVIEW: Run and check UI flows: YAML files of steps with expectations.

USAGE: macos-harness flow <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

SUBCOMMANDS:
  run                     Run flows; failures save a screenshot, the UI tree and the step log.
  check                   Check flow files for mistakes without running them.
  export                  Turn a journal session into a flow; typed text becomes ${text_N}
                          variables to fill in.

  See 'macos-harness help flow <subcommand>' for detailed help.
```

## macos-harness flow run

```text
OVERVIEW: Run flows; failures save a screenshot, the UI tree and the step log.

USAGE: macos-harness flow run <paths> ... [--var <var> ...] [--junit <junit>] [--artifacts <artifacts>] [--record <record>] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <paths>                 Flow files, or folders of .yaml files.

OPTIONS:
  --var <var>             name=value for a ${name} variable (repeatable).
  --junit <junit>         Write a JUnit XML report here.
  --artifacts <artifacts> Folder for failure artifacts (private flows use
                          ~/Library/Logs/macos-harness/flow-results). (default: flow-results)
  --record <record>       Record the flow's app: off, failures (keep the movie when a flow fails)
                          or always. (values: off, failures, always; default: off)
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness flow check

```text
OVERVIEW: Check flow files for mistakes without running them.

USAGE: macos-harness flow check <paths> ... [--var <var> ...]

ARGUMENTS:
  <paths>                 Flow files, or folders of .yaml files.

OPTIONS:
  --var <var>             name=value for a ${name} variable (repeatable).
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness flow export

```text
OVERVIEW: Turn a journal session into a flow; typed text becomes ${text_N} variables to fill in.

USAGE: macos-harness flow export <session> [--name <name>] [--out <out>] [--journal <journal>]

ARGUMENTS:
  <session>               Session ID from `macos-harness journal`, or `last`.

OPTIONS:
  --name <name>           The flow's name (default: the session ID).
  --out <out>             Write the flow here instead of printing it.
  --journal <journal>     Journal folder to read (default: this build's).
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness record

```text
OVERVIEW: Record an app's windows to a movie, and pull stills out of it.

USAGE: macos-harness record <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.

SUBCOMMANDS:
  start                   Start recording an app's windows (only that app's) until `record stop` or
                          the time limit.
  stop                    Stop a recording (or all of yours) and finish the file.
  frames                  Save stills from a movie as PNGs, one every --every seconds.

  See 'macos-harness help record <subcommand>' for detailed help.
```

## macos-harness record start

```text
OVERVIEW: Start recording an app's windows (only that app's) until `record stop` or the time limit.

USAGE: macos-harness record start --app <app> [--window <window>] [--out <out>] [--max-seconds <max-seconds>] [--json]

OPTIONS:
  -a, --app <app>         App name, bundle ID or pid; sim:<device> for an iOS Simulator;
                          android:<device> for an Android emulator or phone.
  -w, --window <window>   Window ID from `windows`; defaults to the focused window.
  --out <out>             Where to write the .mov (default: recording-<app>-<time>.mov here).
  --max-seconds <max-seconds>
                          Stop on its own after this many seconds. (default: 600.0)
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness record stop

```text
OVERVIEW: Stop a recording (or all of yours) and finish the file.

USAGE: macos-harness record stop [<id>] [--json]

ARGUMENTS:
  <id>                    Recording ID from `record start`; omit to stop all of yours.

OPTIONS:
  --json                  Print JSON instead of text.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness record frames

```text
OVERVIEW: Save stills from a movie as PNGs, one every --every seconds.

USAGE: macos-harness record frames <movie> [--every <every>] [--out <out>]

ARGUMENTS:
  <movie>                 The .mov file.

OPTIONS:
  --every <every>         Seconds between stills. (default: 1.0)
  --out <out>             Folder for the PNGs (default: next to the movie).
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness setup

```text
OVERVIEW: Connect an agent: register the MCP server with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI or
opencode, or install the skill for pi.

Shows what it will change and asks first. Without an agent, shows what's set up.

USAGE: macos-harness setup [<agent>] [--yes]

ARGUMENTS:
  <agent>                 claude, codex, cursor, gemini, opencode or pi. (values: claude, codex,
                          cursor, gemini, opencode, pi)

OPTIONS:
  --yes                   Apply without asking (for scripts and agents, after asking the user
                          yourself).
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```

## macos-harness mcp

```text
OVERVIEW: Run as an MCP server on stdin/stdout (for Claude Code, Codex and other MCP hosts).

--background-only keeps the agent off the real mouse and keyboard and stops it bringing apps to the
front, for agents that run while you work (a scheduled job, say); steps that would need them fail
with error 1005 instead. MACOS_HARNESS_BACKGROUND_ONLY=1 does the same for the CLI.

USAGE: macos-harness mcp [--background-only]

OPTIONS:
  --background-only       Never use the real mouse or keyboard or bring apps to the front; refuse
                          steps that would.
  --version               Show the version.
  -h, --help              Show help information.
```
